references.text: The high priest shall not let his hair hang loose or tear his clothes in mourning. This shows that the prohibition against mourning rituals for priests was a permanent arrangement.
Ezekiel gives similar instructions to priests not to show common signs of mourning, such as letting their hair down or tearing their clothes.
The context for this verse - Nadab and Abihu died when they offered strange fire before the Lord.
Moses warns that the Lord's anger may strike the whole congregation, just as he warns Aaron and his sons here.
The Nazirite was not to let his hair hang loose or cut it, which shows that the hair had symbolic meaning in holy contexts.
The priests were to wear their garments properly to avoid bringing guilt upon themselves and dying, a similar warning given to Aaron and his sons.
The tribe of Levi was blessed for priestly service and was to put the Lord's service before family ties.
